transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. But honestly, most days I just have a cup of coffee and a piece of toast in the morning. Then maybe some soup or a few vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary at my age, you know? I don't really see the problem, but she insisted I come in.
Have you noticed any unintentional weight loss or changes in your appetite recently?

Well, my regular doctor did tell me recently that the number on the scale has gotten a bit too low. So I suppose I have lost some weight. But honestly, I don't really see it as a bad thing. To me, being lighter just makes it easier to get around the garden. It helps me keep up on my walks, too. I just don't need to eat as much to keep going as I used to, so it feels pretty natural to me.
Do you ever feel like you don't want to eat at all, even when it's time for your favorite foods?

Well, no, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy my favorites. If my wife makes a nice pot roast or something I really like, I'll definitely have some. 

It's not that I don't want to eat at all... I just don't want a huge plate of it. A small portion is usually enough for me now. So, I still like the taste of things, I just don't feel the need to eat very much of them.
Have you been feeling sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, I can't say that I have. I don't feel sad or down at all. I still enjoy my days just fine. I get out in the garden, go for my walks, read the paper... I haven't lost interest in any of that. 

My mood is perfectly fine, really. Life is pretty good. It's just the eating part that my wife seems to be so worried about.
Have you been experiencing any physical problems, like difficulty chewing, swallowing, or a change in your sense of taste or smell?

No, nothing like that. My teeth are fine, and I don't have any trouble swallowing. Food still tastes and smells exactly the same as it always has. I just don't have the appetite for a lot of it, that's all. Physically, everything works just fine.
Do you ever forget to eat or lose track of meals during the day?

No, I don't forget. I know when it's breakfast, lunch, and dinner. My wife is always there to remind me anyway, but even if she wasn't, I know what time it is. I just... I sit down at the table and I just don't want to eat much. It's not a memory thing, I just don't have the desire for a full meal.
Have you started any new medications or been diagnosed with any medical conditions recently that might affect your appetite?

No, nothing like that. I haven't started taking any new pills recently, and I haven't been diagnosed with anything new either. Health-wise, everything is pretty much exactly the same as it's been for years. There's just no new medical reason for it, as far as I know.
Do you ever feel hungry before meals, or do you often find yourself not feeling hungry even when it's time to eat?

I don't really get hungry beforehand. When it's time to eat, I just... I don't have that feeling. I sit down at the table because it's mealtime, but my stomach isn't rumbling or asking for food. The actual hunger just isn't really there anymore.
Do you ever feel like you have no interest in eating at all, even in between meals or when snacks are offered?

Well, yeah, pretty much. I just don't have much interest in food at all right now. Even between meals, if my wife offers me a snack or a biscuit with my coffee, I usually just wave it off. 

I certainly don't go looking for anything in the cupboards on my own. It's just... I don't know, food just doesn't really appeal to me much these days.
Do you find that you don't take pleasure or enjoyment in things that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or even small daily pleasures?

No, not really. I still enjoy my day-to-day life just fine. I still like... well, working out in the yard, watching my shows, seeing the grandkids when they come by. I still get pleasure out of all those normal things. It's really just the food that I don't care for right now. Everything else is pretty much the same.
Have you noticed any other changes in your body or energy levels that might explain why you're eating less now compared to before?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My energy is still pretty good for my age. I mean, I'm not running marathons or anything, but I don't feel tired or weak during the day, and I'm not feeling sick. My body feels fine, honestly. It's just... I just don't have the appetite I used to, and I couldn't tell you why.
Has there been any specific reason or situation that you can point to that made your appetite change, or has it just been happening without any clear cause?

No, there hasn't been any big event or reason I can think of. It just... sort of happened on its own. I haven't been sick, no major stress or anything like that. I just woke up one day, well, maybe not one day, but over time, I just realized I wasn't hungry anymore. There's no real cause that I can point a finger at.
Do you still take pleasure in the act of eating itself, or does it just feel like something you have to do without any real enjoyment?

It really just feels like something I have to do. I don't get any enjoyment out of it anymore. I mean, I know I need to put something in my stomach, so I try to, but... no, there's no pleasure in it. It's just become a chore.
How long have you felt this way about food — when did you first notice that your appetite started to change?

I'm really not sure. It's hard to pin down an exact time. It didn't happen all at once, you know? I just... gradually noticed I wasn't finishing my meals as much, and it sort of went from there. I couldn't give you a specific date or even a month, honestly. I just haven't kept track of it.
Has your lack of interest in food and eating been present nearly every day for most of the day, without much variation?

Yeah, pretty much. It's just... a constant thing now. Every day, from morning till night, I just don't have any interest in it. It doesn't really come and go or change depending on the time of day. It's just always like that.
